content: (The location is now Solitude.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Lydia, Serana, Frea, chicken, chicken)
Octieve San: What in Oblivion are you doing out here at this hour, you old beggar?
(The location is now The Winking Skeever.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Serana, Lydia, Frea, Corpulus Vinius, Belrand)
Gulum-Ei: Hmph, this early morning chill in the Skeever's got nothing on the frost out by the docks. You nursing that mug all night, old man? Looks like the fire's barely keeping the ghosts away.

(*You are observing the following:* In the dimly lit stone chamber, ancient walls of weathered masonry rise around a central vault door etched with intricate Nordic runes, flanked by flickering braziers that cast warm, dancing shadows across scattered wooden shelves laden with dusty leather-bound tomes, glass vials of shimmering potions, and iron-bound scrolls. A low stone hearth crackles with a modest fire in the corner, illuminating a nearby workbench cluttered with alchemical tools, quills, and inkwells, while arched alcoves recede into the gloom, revealing hints of further shelves stocked with faded maps and peculiar artifacts, evoking the hush of a forgotten library or sanctum deep within a mountain hold.)
(The location is now Solitude.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, Serana, Sorex Vinius, Jaree-Ra, chicken)

Lydia: This city is too quiet for my liking. Too many fancy folk and even fancier guards sticking their noses where they don't belong. Noster Eagle-Eye: Quiet? Ha! You ain't seen the back alleys after dark, lass. I been sleepin' in 'em for three winters now. Plenty of noise if you know where to listen. Lydia: I fought dragons and Thalmor.

Lydia: By Ysmir, look at that sky. The Nords say the aurora is the glow from Sovngarde, shining down to guide brave souls. I half expect to see the Longhouse Embers floating among those lights. Noster Eagle-Eye: Aye, it's purty enough to make a man forget his empty belly for a moment. But beauty don't fill no stomach, and it don't stop Jaree-Ra from skimming coin from the fish barrels down at the docks. Lydia: That Argonian? I've seen his type in Windhelm. Slippery as a fish himself.
Lydia: That Sorex fellow seems eager to pawn his work off on strangers. Still, heading to the Blue Palace could be useful. Jarl Elisif is easily swayed by kind words and a full bottle.

Noster Eagle-Eye: Aye, and a pretty face like yours might get you further than a bottle of rum ever could. Jarl Elisif's got a soft spot for strong Nord women. I've seen her watching the guards drill. Lydia: Flattery from a beggar? I'll take it as a compliment. But I'm sworn to MJR, not to playing politics with a weeping widow. Let's get that rum to Falk Firebeard before I decide to crack it open myself.

Noster Eagle-Eye: Well now, what's this? Your man's shedding his armor like a snake in summer, and there's two lasses all painted up under the aurora. Seems the night's taking a turn I didn't expect. Lydia: By Talos, what is he doing?

Lydia: What in Oblivion is he doing? Those women... I don't like this one bit. Noster Eagle-Eye: Looks like your man's about to have a different kind of adventure, lass. The kind that don't need steel or shouts. I'd wager he's got his eye on more than just Jarl Elisif's rum.

Lydia: I'm going to see what he's about. If those painted harlots try anything, they'll feel my greatsword. Noster Eagle-Eye: Suit yourself, lass. I'll be here, countin' stars and wishin' for a warm hearth. You watch your back now.

(The location is now The Winking Skeever.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Erdi, Daegon, Lisette, Vivienne Onis, Minette Vinius) (Sorex Vinius rested on / used a(n) Chair) (MJR: Hello; Sorex Vinius: New in town, right? If you need a place to sleep, head over to the Winking Skeever. We keep a fine inn. MJR: Who's in charge of Solitude?; Sorex Vinius: Jarl Elisif the Fair. Poor woman. Losing her husband and king like that. It was a dark day for us all. Damn. That reminds me. I have a delivery to make to her steward, Falk Firebeard. He ordered a special bottle of Stros M'Kai Rum. MJR: I can deliver that for you.; Sorex Vinius: Save me a lot of trouble. Here. Take it to the Blue Palace. MJR: So you work in the Winking Skeever?; Sorex Vinius: Work in it? I own it. MJR: ...; Sorex Vinius: Well... okay. My father owns the Winking Skeever. But it's the family business, so it'll be mine when he kicks off.)

Sorex Vinius: Well, that delivery's off my hands. Good riddance. I swear Falk Firebeard gets more demanding each month. Fihada: Demanding? Try courting a Nord woman whose father wants a bow carved from a single piece of yew with no knots. That's demanding. Corpulus Vinius: You two complain like milk-drinkers. I've run this inn through wars, plagues, and a dragon attack that singed half the roof. You just have to pour ale and bend wood. Noster Eagle-Eye: Aye, and some of us have to bend our backs for every scrap of bread. You ever try sleepin' in the alleys near the docks with Jaree-Ra skimming coin from honest folks? Sorex Vinius: Jaree-Ra? That Argonian's been trouble since before I was tall enough to reach the taps.

(Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Eris, Daegon, Gisli, Ahtar, Serana) (Corpulus Vinius rested on / used a(n) Wooden Bar Stool) (Sorex Vinius stood up from a(n) Chair) (Fihada stood up from a(n) Chair)

(Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, Serana, Lisette, Lydia, Minette Vinius) (The location is now Solitude.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Lydia, Serana, Gulum-Ei, Solitude Guard, Jaree-Ra)

Solitude Guard: Traveling this late? On a cold night like this, you two must have business in Solitude. Or trouble. Noster Eagle-Eye: Trouble follows some folks closer than their own shadow. Me, I just watch from the shadows. That's all that's left for a broken scout with one eye and empty pockets. Daegon: Broken scouts and bored guards make for delightful company.

Daegon: That tower is the Blue Palace. Been there once. Full of Jarls and sycophants polishing Dibella's statues while pretending not to stare at the guards in their Imperial Light Bikini armor. Solitude Guard: Watch your tongue, elf. That armor is regulation for the night watch. Keeps us nimble and intimidating. Besides, the goddess appreciates the devotion. Noster Eagle-Eye: Intimidating? I've been sleeping in alleys for years, and the only thing that scares me is an empty bottle. Though I do recall Jaree-Ra over there skimming coin from the docks last I checked. Solitude Guard: Jaree-Ra? That Argonian's been clean for months. Or clean enough that we can't prove otherwise.

Noster Eagle-Eye: A rabbit, wandering this close to the city walls at night? Even the beasts know better than to trust Solitude's kindness. Still, it's a better companion than most folks I've met. Daegon: I swapped my Flame Cloak for a blade. Never know when a rabbit might turn out to be a werewolf in disguise. Or worse, a Thalmor agent.

Noster Eagle-Eye: That warm light spilling out of the archway there... that's the Winking Skeever. Good ale, bad memories. I used to scout the roads for the Legion, you know. Now I count coins thrown by drunks. Solitude Guard: The Skeever's been quiet tonight. Corpulus must've cut off the tap early. Or Sorex finally drank all the stock himself. Daegon: Warm light and drunk locals.

Daegon: A horse wandering loose at this hour? Someone's either a careless stable hand or they're planning a quick exit from Solitude. I've seen that trick before. Gulum-Ei over there probably has a dozen horses stashed around the city for his little skimming operations.

Noster Eagle-Eye: A horse with no rider at this hour means either a lost soldier or a thief's escape plan. I've seen both in my time scouting. The Legion taught me to read tracks, not that it pays for a warm meal these days. Solitude Guard: If it's a thief's horse, it'll be outside the city walls by dawn. My duty is to keep the gate secure, not chase loose livestock. Though if you ask me, that Argonian Gulum-Ei has more horses than he lets on.

Daegon: This whole city reeks of deals made in shadows and coin purses changing hands under tables. At least out there in the wilderness, the only thing trying to stab you is a wolf, and it doesn't bother with contracts. Solitude Guard: That's the truth. The forest doesn't lie to you like folk do. It just tries to kill you, plain and simple. Noster Eagle-Eye: I've had more honest conversations with the rats in the Skeever's cellar than with half the merchants on this street. Tonight's as good a night as any to find a quiet corner and watch the stars spin. They don't ask for coin.
